outcome: Persistent occiput posterior position at birth
cohort: 76 women with singleton pregnancies at term with fetuses in the occiput posterior position at the beginning of the second stage of labor
finding: In this study of women with fetuses in the occiput posterior position at the beginning of the second stage of labor, a larger chin-to-chest angle and nulliparity were independently associated with persistent occiput posterior position at birth.
mod_finding: Among fetuses that did not rotate spontaneously into an occiput anterior position, 32.1% were delivered via Cesarean.
